**The stop condition, and what it rests on.** S0.43 says *Stop if the interim accessibility baseline is not filed.* The runbook's evidence item 8 holds the steps that produce the note and **no note**. The owner stated on 20 October 2026 that they had signed S0.28, the session has not seen the note, and what the owner reported to the guided passes covers steps 2, 3 and 5 only (the screen reader, motion and size, and the browsers-as-products steps were not reported). The owner's instruction to build S0.43 was taken as their decision to build on their own evidence. **So S0.43 is built and not accepted:** until the note is filed under item 8 the screens are not recorded as accepted against the interim baseline, and nothing here says they are. The automated accessibility checks (axe, WCAG 2.2 A and AA, in three engines) are CI evidence and no substitute for the owner's passes.

**What was built** (paths under `apps/ops-web/src/`; the patterns are [COMPONENT_PATTERNS §12.7 and §42.6](../../design/COMPONENT_PATTERNS.md#127-the-pre-sign-in-screens-as-built-s043)).

| Task| Built |
|---|---|
| S0.43a| `/sign-in` (`app/pages/pre-sign-in/SignInPage.tsx`): email and password, `200` signs the person in on the session the API answered (the store is told, the landing replaces the entry, no second read), `202` holds the challenge in memory and goes to the second step; one refusal for every cause and no locked state. `/sign-in/mfa` (`SignInMfaPage.tsx`): a code, four refusals in four states plus a missing authenticator, the lock told here alone, and a visit with no challenge goes back to the first step |
| S0.43b| `/setup/credential` (`SetupCredentialPage.tsx`): the grant read once from the fragment, the new password with its rule shown and checked the way the contract counts, an ordinary employee told the next step is to sign in, a privileged one taken on to the authenticator; one error for a link that cannot be used (`GrantProblem.tsx`) |
| S0.43c| `/setup/mfa` (`SetupMfaPage.tsx`): the QR code and the key to type by hand together, from the first password or from a re-enrolment link (where opening the page redeems nothing and the person presses "Begin set-up"); `/setup/mfa/complete` (`SetupMfaCompletePage.tsx`): says the next step is an ordinary sign-in and that nobody is signed in |
| Shared| `PreSignInFlowLayout` and `pre-sign-in-flow.ts` (what two screens hand each other, in memory, scoped to the family of addresses); `platform/auth/` (`grant-fragment.ts`, `use-grant-token.ts`, `password-rule.ts`, `pre-sign-in-shape.ts`); `FormPage`; `NoReferrer`; `notice.tsx` (`FormNotice`, `FocusedRegion`); the five operations' rules and the context `unknown-outcome` in `problem-copy.ts`; `emptyField` in `use-submission.ts`; the `scope` option of `useTransientSecret`; and `AppFrame`'s move of focus made in a layout effect (ruling 7) |
| Tests| a test for every file above; the nine interface states of each screen (`describeInterfaceStates`); `pre-sign-in-neutral-frame.test.tsx` (no shell in any state); `pre-sign-in-secret-hygiene.test.tsx` (the sentinel search through the real screens); `test/pre-sign-in-contract.test.ts` (each guard held to its schema); `test/browser/pre-sign-in.spec.ts` with its stand-in API; the three end-to-end specs of finding 2 of [§7.35](#735-carried-from-s038-and-s039-23-october-2026) edited |

**Decisions and rulings** (each is mine; none is a product decision).

1. **What two screens hand each other is held in the memory of a layout route, never in the router's state.** The challenge of a privileged sign-in stands for a password that was proved (a challenge and a stolen code complete a sign-in), and the authenticator's material and its continuation grant are bearer secrets. Router state is the history state, which a reload keeps and the sentinel search looks in. So `PreSignInFlowLayout` holds both as transient secrets scoped to the family of addresses (`/sign-in*` or `/setup/*`): a reload of the second step goes back to the first, and a reload of the authenticator screen finds the one error. **Cost if wrong:** a reload costs the person a retype.
2. **`/setup/mfa/complete` is shown on a marker in the history state** (`{ enrolled: true }`), because it holds no secret: a person who writes it by hand sees a page that says the next step is to sign in, which is true of everyone. A visit without it goes to the sign-in.
3. **The grant is read strictly and judged minimally.** `tokenFromHash` accepts exactly one `token`, made of the characters a link carries, that decodes to printable ASCII of at most 512 characters; it does not require the 43 characters of [SECURITY_DESIGN §14](../../architecture/SECURITY_DESIGN.md), because the server judges the grant and one error answers every grant that is not good. **Cost if wrong:** a malformed link costs a round trip instead of none.
4. **The password step has one refusal, and a refusal it was not told how to word reads as a wrong password.** A `CREDENTIAL_LOCKED`, a `NOT_FOUND` or a `PERMISSION_DENIED` at `staffSignIn` (none of which the contract gives it) shows "The email or password is not correct.", so nothing the server might one day say about an address reaches the screen. A wait, an Origin that could not be verified, a request that got no answer and a refusal of a field are worded as they are.
5. **At the second step, `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` reads as a finished attempt** (the identity stopped being eligible between the steps; the contract lists the code for this operation and no state for it).
6. **The password and the code are emptied after every answer that is not a success**, including a lost connection, and the cursor returns to the field. A retry costs a retype and leaves no password where it was typed.
7. **`AppFrame` moves focus in a layout effect, not a passive one.** The move to the new page's heading was made after the browser had painted the page, so for a few milliseconds the new form was on the screen and typable while focus was still where the old page left it: a field filled at that moment (a quick typist, a password manager, a test) lost its text. A WebKit test failed one run in eight on it; the cause was found by logging the focus events, pinned by a deterministic test that reads the focus at the moment the form's markup is committed (it failed in Chromium and WebKit, and passes in all three engines after the change), and the previously flaky tests then passed 270 repeated runs. The change is to a foundation component the owner approved in S0.38; it changes when, not whether, focus moves.
8. **The sign-in screen asks for no session.** A signed-in person who opens `/sign-in` sees the form; signing in again replaces their session. Reading the session to redirect them would put a request on the wire from a pre-sign-in page, which S0.38 decided not to do.
9. **There is no "confirm password" field** on `/setup/credential`: the specification names none, and the field has the "Show password" button. A mistyped password costs the person a recovery. The owner may want one.
10. **A challenge is held for the longest a page holds a secret (15 minutes), not until its `expires_at`.** The server decides the five minutes; the client's clock is not asked to agree with it, so a skewed clock cannot make a good challenge look expired.
11. **All wording is proposed for review**, in `problem-copy.ts` and in the pages: the sign-in's refusal and its wait; the four refusals of the second step and the missing authenticator; the one error of a link and its two ways on; the rule of a new password; the lost-answer sentences of the three link operations, each of which says what to try next; the authenticator screen's instructions; the confirmation. Customer-facing wording is a Product Owner input (COMPONENT_PATTERNS §33).

**Findings for the owner.**

1. **S0.28's note is not filed** (above). The screens are built and not accepted.
2. **No link to recovery.** The lock message says "Recovering the password clears it", and `/recovery` and `/recovery/complete` are the recovery slice's, so there is nothing to link to ("does not link to a screen that does not exist").
3. **The second step has no "start again" control** while the form is shown; the person uses the browser's Back or waits for an ending. The contract's four states do not include one, and adding it is a one-line change that the owner may want.
4. **The reference of a failed request is shown only when the server failed** (an unavailable answer), so a person can quote it; it is never shown beside a refused password.
5. **The authenticator screen cannot be recovered by the person once the material is gone** (a reload, leaving, 15 minutes): it shows the one error. For an ordinary onboarding the way back is an administrator's (`resetStaffMfa`); for a bootstrap administrator it is the provisioning command (AC-SLICE-000-93). The screen offers nothing it cannot do.
6. **`GBT-W16`'s page half only.** The grant is read once and removed by replacing the entry, opening a page redeems nothing, and the redeeming `fetch` carries the real `Origin`, no `Referer` and the grant in its body alone, in three engines against a stand-in API. The run against the real API over HTTPS is S0.46 (E, not run).
7. **A foundation component changed (ruling 7).** The three end-to-end specs (`journey.spec.ts`, `https-trust.spec.ts`, `browser-boundary.spec.ts`) now assert the real sign-in screen; `https-trust.spec.ts` belongs to `test:e2e:https`, which is not run here, so its one added line is unproven until the first hosted run.
8. **`/recovery` and `/recovery/complete`** (the other two of the seven pre-authentication routes) are not built; they are not in S0.43's five.
9. **The `data:` URI hazard did not arise** (the QR is an inline SVG), and **the production bundle now holds the QR encoder** (`uqr`), because the authenticator screen is its first caller outside the showcase; the decoder (`jsqr`) is still absent (a build test).

**Evidence.** Component tests on the Ops Portal's jsdom project, one file for each screen and for each piece they share: `SignInPage`, `SignInMfaPage`, `SetupCredentialPage`, `SetupMfaPage` and `SetupMfaCompletePage` (states, what each sends, what each shows for each answer, and their nine interface states through `describeInterfaceStates`); `PreSignInFlowLayout` and `pre-sign-in-flow` (what is handed over, and when it is let go of); `use-grant-token` (the fragment read once, the entry replaced, development's strict mode, letting go at completion, navigation, expiry, hiding and a session change), `grant-fragment`, `password-rule` and `pre-sign-in-shape`; the `scope` option of `useTransientSecret`; `emptyField`; the copy table (`pre-sign-in-copy.test.ts`, which also refuses any wording at the password step that names a lock, an account or a status); `pre-sign-in-neutral-frame.test.tsx` (no navigation, sign-out, session data or session read in any state of any of the five); and `pre-sign-in-secret-hygiene.test.tsx`, which drives the real application with a planted password, grant, seed, continuation grant, challenge reference and code and searches the query and mutation caches, both storages, the cookies, the address, the history state, the title, the console, the requests and the page, at completion, expiry, navigation, `pagehide`, a refusal and a session change, and with a seed whose answer arrives late. `test/pre-sign-in-contract.test.ts` reads the contract and holds each response guard to its schema, and the five operations to be anonymous pre-session ones at the paths the pages use. In a browser (`test/browser/pre-sign-in.spec.ts`, against the production build and against the development server, with a stand-in API that records the headers it was sent): the fragment read once and removed by replacing the entry (Back and Forward find no grant), nothing sent by opening a page, the redeeming `fetch` with the real `Origin`, no `Referer` and the grant in its body alone; the sign-in of an ordinary and of a privileged employee, the four refusals of the second step, the single refusal of the first; the QR code **decoded from what the browser painted** (the independent decoder, from a screenshot) to the whole URI, beside the same key, shown once and gone on a reload and on leaving; the picture at three pixels to a module or more at 320 px; the keyboard order and the focus ring of the sign-in; the form within the form measure; the frame's focus at the moment the next form exists; and axe (WCAG 2.2 A and AA), no sideways scrolling and no shell for each of thirteen states at 1280, 768 and 320 px. The spec turns tracing, screenshots and video off for its own contexts, because its pages type and receive credential-shaped values. Tests were written before the code that satisfies them; **the page tests were not each watched failing first** (their modules did not exist when they were written), so the evidence that they can fail is the break campaign below, and the tests I did watch fail for the right reason are the `scope` option (2 of 7), the frame's focus (red in Chromium and WebKit before the change) and the WebKit flake that found it.

**Targeted breaks** (the real source changed, the tests that should catch it run, each file restored and checked by hash): **43 breaks of the unit and component guards, all caught.** Reading my own list before running it showed four guards that the first tests could not see (the two "leaving" flags that stop a page calling its own link bad for the instant before the route changes, the material kept in memory after a refused grant, and the second step's race with the clearing of its challenge), and their tests were written first; one break, the name of the setup family, changes nothing observable and was caught only once a direct test of `familyOf` pinned it. The breaks were of: the fragment reader (characters, control characters, the length boundary), the password rule (the typed count, the normalised count both ways, UTF-16 units), the response guards (a challenge id, "ready" with material, an undrawable address, an unbounded grant), the grant hook (the fragment left in the address, a new history entry, `reading`, the page's own rewriting counted as leaving), the secret's scope, the layout's two scopes, the history-state marker, the first step (every refusal shown as it is, a reference beside a refused password, the password kept, the entry not replaced, the session not recorded, a long password sent, the email trimmed), the second step (a lock told as a finished attempt, the challenge kept, the leaving guard, the entry not replaced, the code unchecked), the credential page (the rule unchecked, the leaving flag), the authenticator page (the leaving flag, the material kept after a refused grant, the marker left out, the answer not judged, the code unchecked), the announcement of a notice, the referrer policy and two sentences of copy. **Nine breaks of the browser-only guards**, in Chromium: the frame's focus moved after the paint, a referrer policy that sends the origin, the fragment left in the address, a new history entry for it, a form with no measure, the picture drawn from the wrong text, a copy button, and the show-password button out of the tab order were **all caught in the browser**; the ninth, the second step keeping its history entry on success, is caught by the unit test that asserts `REPLACE` and was not asserted in the browser.

**The gate of the final tree** (uncached, `TURBO_FORCE=true`, Node 24.21.0, Windows, PostgreSQL started by the owner, run once on the tree handed over, after the breaks above and with nothing edited while it ran; the file hashes before and after are identical): `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `build`, `contract:check` (17 operations compared, no findings), `api-client:check`, `db:check`, `pnpm run test:local`, `test:db`, `pnpm audit --audit-level high`, `test:browser` over Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and `test:e2e`: **every command exit 0**. Root 1245 (1243 passed, 2 skipped; unchanged, S0.43 added no root test), Ops **1426 passed in 81 files** (1036 in 64 at S0.42), API 5784 passed and 12 skipped, api-client 250, harness 482 passed and 3 skipped; `test:db` 2888 passed and 2 skipped in 91 files; **browser 644 passed and 4 skipped** (260 and 4 at S0.42: the 384 new are the pre-sign-in spec, 64 tests in each of six projects, three engines against the production build and against the development server; the four skipped are the WebKit forced-colours tests that Playwright cannot emulate); `test:e2e` 20 passed; the audit exits 0 and still reports the one moderate esbuild advisory. The production bundle is 405.66 kB (127.02 kB gzipped), up from about 359 kB: the authenticator screen is the QR encoder's first caller outside the showcase, so the encoder is now in the bundle, and the test-only decoder is not (a build test). **Not run:** every hosted Linux and HTTPS check (needs the owner's push), `test:e2e:https` (so the one line added to `https-trust.spec.ts` is unproven until the first hosted run), a real sign-in through the real API over HTTPS (S0.45), `GBT-W16` against the real API in the engines (S0.46), the owner's accessibility passes, Safari and anything on a handset.

**Cautions learned.** (1) A move of focus made in a passive effect runs after the paint: a field filled in that gap types into nothing (found as a WebKit test failing one run in eight; the cause was found by logging `focusin` and `input` events in the page, not by raising a timeout). (2) A page that empties the secret it holds in order to leave must not render "not found" on its way out: both second steps keep a `leaving` flag. (3) Prettier and ESLint rewrite `!-~` in a regular expression to `!-~`; a break script must match the formatted file. (4) `[...text]` on a string is refused by the lint rule `no-misused-spread`; `Array.from(text)` counts code points. (5) The router types the history state as `any`: read it as `const state: unknown = useLocation().state`. (6) A thrown render error is caught by the router's own boundary, so test a hook's throw outside the router. (7) `pnpm exec playwright` fails under Git Bash on this machine; run it from PowerShell inside `apps/ops-web`.

### 7.40 Carried from S0.44 (24 October 2026)

**Status.** **Built** on the same uncommitted, unstaged, unpushed tree (HEAD `825ec2f`), on the owner's instruction of 24 October 2026 ("Great continue and build S0.44 to completion. A perfect intuitive design"), after S0.43 ([§7.39](#739-carried-from-s043-24-october-2026)), which is still **built and not accepted** because the owner's accessibility note (S0.28) is not filed under the runbook's evidence item 8; S0.44 builds on that tree and does not change that. The standing rules held: no stage, commit, push, reset or stash, no dependency added, nothing after S0.44, and PostgreSQL was started by the owner. Only `apps/ops-web`, the one `design/` document the patterns live in, and the plan changed: the API, the contract, the database and the generated client did not. The plan is the one progress record: no handoff file.

**What was built** (paths under `apps/ops-web/src/`; the patterns are [COMPONENT_PATTERNS §12.8 and §42.7](../../design/COMPONENT_PATTERNS.md#128-the-six-signed-in-identity-screens-as-built-s044)).

| Task| Built |
|---|---|

| S0.44b| `/admin/staff/new` (`StaffCreatePage.tsx`): name, email, phone, role (chosen by name from `listAssignableStaffRoleBundles`, with the note on the roles that need a Platform Admin) and hub; no password, status or creator; sent under an `Idempotency-Key`, so a lost answer is tried again under the same key; the success says a different person must approve it. `/admin/staff/{id}` (`StaffDetailPage.tsx`): the profile and the version it was read at, approve (`ConfirmationDialog`), reject, send a new setup link (reason dialogs), and the links on to the reset and to the person's sessions; every act sends the `ETag` exactly as read, a conflict is explained and the profile read again, a profile outside the hubs and one that does not exist are pages of their own |

**Decisions and rulings** (each is mine; none is a product decision).

1. **Recovery of a credential is not offered.** `ops-portal.md` §7 lists "start exceptional recovery" on `/admin/staff/{id}`, and `recoverStaffCredential` is not built in the API (`implemented-scope.ts`). A button for it would be a success stub, which the rules forbid, so the profile offers what exists: approve, reject, a new first setup link, the reset of an authenticator, the sessions. **Cost if wrong:** one more button when the operation is built.
2. **The landing's heading and title stay "Melarc Ops Portal"**; the menu's label is "Overview" (the owner's decision of 24 October). Changing the heading would touch six tests and every screen's way back for no gain in clarity.
3. **`/admin/sessions` is in the menu, and a profile leads to it with the person chosen** (changed on 25 October 2026: it had no entry and could not be reached, [§7.41](#741-carried-from-the-real-stack-audit-of-s044-25-october-2026)). The list is asked for one principal (`principal_type` and `principal_id` are required), so opened from the menu the page asks for a person first and says how to choose one. Riders have no screen yet, so their sessions cannot be reached until one links here.
4. **A profile is read once, and the page acts on that version.** `WithProfile` gives the page the read itself: a second observer of a query that is stale the moment it is read refetched on mount, and a version read twice changes under the person's hand. The reads are not repeated on focus or on reconnect (every accepted request counts as activity), are not kept once the screen lets go (`gcTime: 0`), and a failed one is retried by the person, as the reason catalogue's is.
5. **The conflict sentences say the causes the contract gives.** For a reset, `STATE_CONFLICT` is a record that moved *or* a record with no factor to reset, and the contract gives the screen no way to tell which: the sentence says both and offers to read the record again. For a re-issue the contract names two causes and no version check (a password already set, or a bootstrap administrator), and the sentence says exactly those ([§7.41](#741-carried-from-the-real-stack-audit-of-s044-25-october-2026), defect 4).
6. **Approving is a confirmation and rejecting is a reason.** The contract asks for a reason only on rejection, and approving gives access and does no harm, so `ConfirmationDialog` confirms in the primary treatment; the reason dialogs keep the danger treatment except the new setup link, which takes `confirmVariant="primary"`.
7. **Ending a session is safe to send again, and a session already gone reads as done.** `revokeSession` takes no key, but ending an ended session is no harm (ops-portal.md §7), so it offers *Try again* as well as *Check the record*, and `404` is "That session had already ended". The other eight reason operations offer the record only ([§7.38](#738-carried-from-s040-to-s042-24-october-2026) ruling 2).
8. **The primary hub is optional, as the schema has it**; a person who acts in one hub places the profile in it, and anyone else chooses or leaves "No primary hub". **Cost if wrong:** one default.
9. **The role column and the role's name appear only when the session may read the assignable roles** (`permission.assignable_bundle.read`). A reader who may not sees no role rather than "Another role" on every row, and no id is ever shown.
10. **The maker's own profile says so (changed 25 October 2026, [§7.42](#742-carried-from-the-owners-decisions-of-25-october-2026): a Platform Admin may decide it and the session lists no tier, so the page offers the maker the acts with a note, and the server decides).** `principal_id` is carried from the session so that "You created this profile, so a different person has to approve or reject it" replaces the buttons. It is a hint: the server refuses `SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN` whatever the page shows. The same for resetting one's own authenticator.
11. **`formatInstant` is 24-hour in Accra with a fixed table of months**, because one ICU release spells September "Sept" and the screen must not change with the runtime. A browser test shows it with the machine in another zone.
12. **The menu marks the most specific entry current** (`currentItem`). "Add a staff profile" lies under "Staff", and the first real nested entries marked both; a profile's page keeps "Staff" current. Found by a real-browser test.
13. **The heading of a profile page is one element from loading to loaded** (`WithProfile` owns it), and a page of its own (not found, outside the hubs) takes the focus the heading had. A heading rebuilt when the profile arrived dropped the focus the frame had put on it; found by a real-browser test, pinned by a jsdom one.
14. **No empty-state "Add a staff profile" beside the header's**; the one way to add is where it always is.
15. **All wording is proposed for review**, in `staff-copy.ts` and the pages: the three refusals of authority at approving, the failed delivery ("Nothing was changed… try again once it is"), the conflict sentences, the sentences of each status, the reset's explanation ("You will not see the link"), the sessions page's guidance. Customer-facing wording is a Product Owner input (COMPONENT_PATTERNS §33).

**Findings for the owner.**

1. **S0.28's note is not filed**, so S0.43 is not accepted and S0.44's screens rest on the same unrecorded baseline.
2. **`recoverStaffCredential` is not built** (ruling 1): the profile has no recovery action. It is on the specification's row for the profile.
3. **The sessions page cannot be reached for a rider** until a rider screen links to it, and no screen lists a vendor's.
4. **The list has no total.** The API returns a page and a token, not a count; the page says what it shows and whether more follow.
5. **A profile shows no names of who created or approved it**: the contract carries ids only, so the page can say "you created this" and nothing more.
6. **A profile outside the hubs is a page of its own** whose copy names no hub (the contract does not say which).
7. **In Safari's engine a click does not focus a button**, so a dialog opened by a click has nothing to give focus back to; opened from the keyboard it does. The browser test opens it from the keyboard for that reason (the dialogs spec does the same). Nothing to fix.
8. **A real sign-in over HTTPS, and the screens against the real API, are S0.45 and S0.46** (E, not run). Everything here ran against a stand-in that is stateful but is not the API.
9. **On a narrow screen the sessions table scrolls sideways** inside its named, focusable region (the table pattern), so the "End session" column is off to the right at 360 px and a keyboard reaches it through the region; a card layout for narrow widths is a design decision the table pattern does not make.
10. **Test timing on a busy machine.** The first test of a jsdom file pays for the first render and, with the machine loaded by other programs, can take longer than Testing Library's one second; no timeout was raised and no check loosened, and the one test that did it uses a cheaper query first.

The spec turns tracing, screenshots and video off for its own contexts, because its pages hold credential-shaped values. **I looked at every screen myself** in Chromium at 1280 and 360 px (screenshots under the git-ignored `tmp/screens-s044/`, synthetic data) and fixed what I saw: the gap under "What you can do", the stacked facts of a profile, a name broken in the middle of a word in the list; the screenshots are not evidence of anything the tests do not show. Tests were written before the code that satisfies them; **the page tests were not each watched failing first** (their modules did not exist when they were written), so the evidence that they can fail is the break campaign below.

**Targeted breaks** (the real source changed, the tests that should catch it run, each file restored and checked by hash): **86 breaks of the unit and component guards. 78 were caught at once and eight were not, and the eight were each looked at.** Five were real weak spots and were closed with a test that was then shown to catch the break: a note dropped on its way from a dialog to the request (the four screens that send one now each assert it), a read that is repeated when the window is focused or the connection returns (a test that dispatches the events Query actually listens for), a profile, list or session kept after its screen lets go, a search read out of the address with its spaces, and an exact count claimed for a queue that runs past its page. One was dead code and was removed: the create page keyed its form on a counter, but the form is already gone once a profile is created, so "Add another" always draws a new one. **Two are equivalent mutants and are left**: the version a command holds (`command.version`) equals the version of the render in every flow a person can reach, because none of the acts that take it can be sent again, so `command.version ?? etag` and `etag` cannot be told apart through a screen; the component tests of both dialogs assert that the version the person saw is the one sent. browser test drives (Cancel is the approval dialog's first control, so the browser focuses it without the marker) and matters for the reason dialog, whose focus S0.41's dialogs spec proves.

**The gate of the final tree** (uncached, `TURBO_FORCE=true`, Node 24.21.0, Windows, PostgreSQL started by the owner, run once on the tree handed over, with nothing edited while it ran; the file hashes before and after are identical): `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `build`, `contract:check` (17 operations compared, no findings), `api-client:check`, `db:check`, `pnpm run test:local`, `test:db`, `pnpm audit --audit-level high`, `test:browser` over Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and `test:e2e`: **every command exit 0**. Root 1245 (1243 passed, 2 skipped; unchanged, S0.44 added no root test), Ops **1954 passed in 96 files** (1426 in 81 at S0.43), API 5784 passed and 12 skipped, api-client 250, harness 482 passed and 3 skipped; `test:db` 2888 passed and 2 skipped in 91 files; **browser 960 passed and 6 skipped** (644 and 4 at S0.43: the 316 new are the staff spec, 53 tests in each of six projects, three engines against the production build and against the development server; the two new skipped are the test that Tab reaches the primary link in WebKit, which Playwright for Windows cannot run, and the four earlier ones are still the WebKit forced-colours tests); `test:e2e` 20 passed; the audit exits 0 and still reports the one moderate esbuild advisory. The production bundle is 475.20 kB (145.68 kB gzipped), up from 405.66 kB: six screens, the data layer and the dialog. **It was run three times.** The first stopped at its first test stage because this plan linked to this section before the section existed (three anchors); its database stage, which had already started when it was stopped, failed in two rate-limiter tests whose child process could not start (Windows exit 0xC0000142, with that stopped run's leftovers on the machine) and passed on the next run. The second was green apart from three browser tests: S0.41's dialogs spec asserted the generic conflict sentence for the showcase's reset demo, whose conflict is now worded for the operation (the same assertion in the dialog's jsdom tests had been corrected earlier); the spec was corrected and the third run, recorded here, is green throughout. **Not run:** every hosted Linux and HTTPS check (needs the owner's push), `test:e2e:https`, a real sign-in and these screens against the real API over HTTPS (S0.45), `GBT-W16` against the real API in the engines (S0.46), the owner's accessibility passes, Safari and anything on a handset.

**Cautions learned.** (1) A heading rebuilt when data arrives drops the focus the frame put on it: keep the heading in one component across loading and loaded, and give a page of its own the focus the heading had. (2) A second observer of a stale query refetches on mount: hand the read down. (3) `test/no-duplicate-wire-types.test.ts` refuses a local type named like a contract schema (a type alias too) and pins which files import the browser client: use the `ApiClient` alias of `api-client.tsx` and `isNotFound` of `api-response.ts`. (4) The design-token guard refuses any rule that removes an outline, even the mouse-only one, for a rule that styles focus without drawing one: a programmatically focused `tabindex="-1"` place needs no rule, because the global `:focus-visible` rule draws a ring for a keyboard and not for a mouse. (5) Query listens for `visibilitychange` on the window, which a bare `new Event` on the document never reaches; the event must bubble. (6) The first test of a jsdom file is cold; do not raise a timeout, use a cheaper query first. (7) In Safari's engine a click does not focus a button; open a dialog from the keyboard in a test that follows focus. (8) A script written through Bash loses backslashes: write it with the file tool.

### 7.41 Carried from the real-stack audit of S0.44 (25 October 2026)

**Why.** The owner ran the backend and the Ops Portal and saw only the sign-in page: none of the six screens built in S0.44 could be reached, and what had been said about them had been tested only against the stand-in API of the browser tests. This is the audit that was owed, run against the real API, a real database and a real browser, and what it changed.

**Why nothing could be reached (root cause, found from the API's own log).** The owner's `melarc_dev` was migrated (`db:migrate`: nothing to apply) but had never been given the reference data: `db:seed` had not been run, so the setting `rate_limit_staff_signin` had no approved value and sign-in answered `503` before it looked at a password (`/readyz` was ready all the while: it checks the connection, not the seed). Because the bootstrap administrators are written after the reference seed, none existed either. **Done on the owner's database, on the instruction "fix all the issues":** `db:bootstrap` (roles and database ready), `db:migrate` (nothing applied) and `db:seed` (1 hub, 127 permissions, 6 role bundles, 36 grants, 2 fixed policies, 31 settings, 12 reasons). Nothing else on that database was touched; **no administrator was created** (§7.41 finding 1).

**A second cause behind the first, found only on the owner's own server.** The owner's `apps/api/.env` allows the browser origin `http://127.0.0.1:5173` (`OPS_ORIGIN`, as `.env.example` has it), and `pnpm --filter @melarc/ops-web run dev` listened on Vite's default host, `localhost`, which on that machine is the IPv6 loopback. So the address that loaded the page (`http://localhost:5173`) was refused at every sign-in with `403 CSRF_VALIDATION_FAILED` ("The request could not be verified"), and the address the API allows (`http://127.0.0.1:5173`) did not connect at all: sign-in could not have worked on that setup even with the database seeded. The scratch stack did not show it, because it set its own origin. Shown by sending the same bogus sign-in to the real API: from `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:5173` the answer is `422 INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, from `http://localhost:5173` it is `403`.

**How it was run.** A disposable database made by the project's own tool (`e2e-database create`), the real `db:seed` and `bootstrap:seed` (two scratch custodians), the real API on port 3011, the real Vite development server on 5174, the real delivery worker with a scratch capture folder, and scripts in real Chromium that did what a person does and printed no password, secret or code. Driven: both administrators' whole first journey (the secret of the bundle, a password, an authenticator, sign-in with a code); every screen; a profile added by one administrator, seen waiting by the other, approved, and another rejected with a reason; a stale version (one administrator rejecting what the other had approved); a new setup link; the reset of an authenticator and the person's re-enrolment through the link the worker delivered; ending a session; the invited colleague's journey through the captured link, the menu of an Ops Staff, and the pages they may not open; the signed-out, wrong-password, empty-form, unusable-link, direct second step and unknown-address states; and every screen at 390 px. The scratch stack and its folders were removed afterwards. **Not run against the real stack:** the forbidden state of a Platform Admin's own pages (covered in jsdom and in the browser tests), HTTPS (S0.45), Firefox and WebKit by hand.

**Defects found and fixed, each by a test that failed first** (the fifth is the second root cause above).

1. **The landing said "No hub is listed for your session" to a Platform Admin.** The session lists the hubs of its own (`authorized_hubs`), and the reach that covers every hub is held by grant and is not in that list, so the sentence read as "you reach nothing". It then said "No hub is listed for your session. Access that covers every hub is not listed here." Since the owner's decision of the same day ([§7.42](#742-carried-from-the-owners-decisions-of-25-october-2026)) a session whose grants reach every hub lists them all, so the sentence is again only "No hub is listed for your session."
2. **A choice that could not be made was drawn as one.** The add-profile form's *Primary hub* offered only "No primary hub" to a Platform Admin. With no hub listed the field is now disabled and says "Your session lists no hub to choose from, so this profile is created without one." (finding 2).
3. **`/admin/sessions` could not be reached from the menu.** It now has an entry, *Sessions*, under *Add a staff profile*, for the key it already needed (`staff.read`); the landing lists it. A profile still leads to it with the person chosen, and opened from the menu it asks for a person (ruling 3 of §7.40 is corrected).
4. **A new setup link was offered to someone who could not be sent one.** The profile of an administrator with an authenticator offered *Send a new setup link*, and the real API answered `409`. The contract refuses a re-issue for a profile that already has a password and for a bootstrap administrator, and the operation takes no version check, so the sentence "changed after you opened it … Reload it" was wrong for it. The act is now offered only when the record says `NOT_ELIGIBLE` (no factor exists or is being set up, which only a person with a password can have), and the sentence says the two causes of the contract.
5. **The development server listened where the API refuses to be called from.** `vite.config.ts` now sets `host: '127.0.0.1'`, `port: 5173` and `strictPort: true` (every browser test and the integrated harness already started it so; only the plain `dev` script did not), and `test/dev-server-origin.test.ts` ties the three to `OPS_ORIGIN` of `apps/api/.env.example`, so the two cannot drift again. A running development server restarts itself on this change; the portal is opened at `http://127.0.0.1:5173`, and `DEVELOPMENT.md` and the B0 runbook now say so.

**Seen and not a defect.** The approval dialog is an `alertdialog`, not a `dialog`. "No session was open" after a reset was true (that administrator had signed out). The `404` in the browser console on every page is the browser asking for `/favicon.ico`: the application has no icon (finding 5). Sideways scrolling of the tables on a phone is the approved pattern (COMPONENT_PATTERNS §20: intentional, in a named focusable region) and the specification calls the portal desktop-first (finding 6 of §7.40 stands).

**Findings for the Product Owner.**

1. **There is no preset login, by design, and none was made.** An administrator exists only after `bootstrap:seed` names two custodians (two real identities, written once: a second run refuses, and undoing it needs `db:reset`), and each sets their own password and authenticator from the one-time secret in their bundle. I did not create accounts or invent identities for you, and a password I know would defeat the custody the specification requires. `DEVELOPMENT.md` now has the steps ("First sign-in").
2. **A Platform Admin cannot choose a primary hub, and a profile one makes has none. (Decided and done later the same day: [§7.42](#742-carried-from-the-owners-decisions-of-25-october-2026).)** The session's `authorized_hub_ids` and `authorized_hubs` are empty for an administrator (all-hub reach is carried by the grant, `effective-scope.ts`), and no operation among the 38 lists hubs. By `effective-scope.ts` an own-hub grant reaches only the hubs of the session, so a profile made without a hub reaches none (read from the code, not tried: no hub-scoped screen exists yet). The contract's text ("a principal whose authority covers more hubs than the supported maximum is refused … at session issue") reads as if all-hub authority were listed. **Decide:** list every hub in `authorized_hubs` for an all-hub principal at session issue, or add a list-hubs operation. Until then the form says it plainly.
3. **`/readyz` answers ready while sign-in cannot work. (Decided and done later the same day: [§7.42](#742-carried-from-the-owners-decisions-of-25-october-2026).)** It checks the connection, not the reference seed. A readiness check of the seed (or a clearer log line at start) would have shown the problem at once. Not changed: it is a behaviour of the API's probes.
4. **A Senior Ops person's *Sessions* entry opens a page that can list only riders**, and no rider screen exists to choose one (ops-portal.md §7: a Senior Ops user reads and ends rider sessions only). It will work when the rider screens link to it.
5. **No icon. (A candidate was made for the owner's approval the same day: [§7.42](#742-carried-from-the-owners-decisions-of-25-october-2026).)** Every page makes the browser ask for `/favicon.ico` and get `404`. An icon is a brand asset: the brand README records which logo variants are approved, and none is an icon. Say if one is wanted.
6. **The delivery worker is a separate process.** An approval, a re-sent link and a reset queue a message that reaches the person only while the worker runs (`DEVELOPMENT.md`, section 5). The page says the link "is on its way", which is true of the queue and not of the delivery.

7. **Two Vite servers on one checkout break each other.** A second development server (or a scratch one) shares `apps/ops-web/node_modules/.vite` with a running one, which then answers `504 Outdated Optimize Dep` and shows a blank page until it is restarted. Stop and start your own, and do not run a second beside it.

**Gate on the tree of this audit (25 October 2026; `tmp/gate-s044-main.log`; an earlier run on a tree before the dev-server fix was stopped on purpose, and its tree is not this one).** Every stage exited 0 except lint, which failed on 28 `no-undef` reports, all in the git-ignored helper `tmp/first-admin.mjs` that `eslint .` reaches (it is not in the repository, and a disable directive now stands at its head; the lint of the tree after the later changes is in the gate of [§7.42](#742-carried-from-the-owners-decisions-of-25-october-2026)). Root tests 1245 (1243 passed, 2 skipped); Ops Portal 1960 in 97 files; API 5784 (12 skipped); `api-client` 250; harness 482 (3 skipped); `test:db` 2888 (2 skipped) in 91 files; `test:browser` 966 passed (6 skipped); `test:e2e` 20; `pnpm audit --audit-level high` exit 0 (one moderate advisory); `contract:check` 17 operations, no findings; the production bundle 475.50 kB (145.79 kB gzipped); the tree was unchanged by the gate. **Not run:** the hosted Linux and HTTPS runs, `test:e2e:https`, S0.45 and S0.46, the owner's accessibility passes, Safari and a handset, and Firefox and WebKit by hand. The five `melarc_test_*` databases that this session did not make were listed by `db:orphans` and, on the owner's instruction of the same day, dropped.

**Tests added or changed.** `test/dev-server-origin.test.ts` (new: the dev server's host, port and strict port against `OPS_ORIGIN` of the API example); registry (the sessions entry; `listSessions` guarded by the key of the contract), landing (the new sentence, three places to go), the shell's entries, the add-profile form (a disabled hub field with its reason, and the usual help when a hub is listed), the profile (no new setup link beside an authenticator, in both states; the conflict sentence), the words of the re-issue, `staff.spec.ts` (the menu leads to the sessions page; the setup-link test now uses a profile with no authenticator) and `shell.spec.ts` (the Tab walk has the new entry).

### 7.42 Carried from the owner's decisions of 25 October 2026

**Why.** After the audit of [§7.41](#741-carried-from-the-real-stack-audit-of-s044-25-october-2026) the owner, the same day, had the leftover test databases dropped, decided the open questions of that audit, and corrected a rule: *"Admin which the highest authority should be able to approve anything, it does not need a second Admin to approve. For instance I created a staff and it is asking me to ask the other Admin user to approve. Those approval can be for other users not Admin. Rectify that and fix it including the docs."* Nothing is staged, committed or pushed.

**The decisions** (asked together; the owner chose the recommended option of each of the first three, and, for the favicon, which had no recommended option, the one that derives it from the logo).

1. **Approval: every approval, platform-wide.** A Platform Admin, that is an approver whose **acting grant is at tier P**, approves or rejects a record they made, with no second person, in every maker-checker flow. It is the tier of the grant that authorizes the act, read from the session's snapshot, never a role's name. It lifts the same-actor exclusion and nothing else: the permission, the scope, the state, the reason and the tier a privileged target needs still apply. **Not lifted:** a rule that a person may not act on themselves (nobody resets their own authenticator: `resetStaffMfa` on oneself stays `SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN`, which is why the product keeps two administrators).
2. **Hubs: the session lists every hub** for a principal whose snapshot holds a grant of the all-hub scope (no new operation).
3. **Readiness: `/readyz` is not ready until the reference seed has run.**
4. **Favicon: derive it from the logo, and the owner approves the result before it is used.**

**What changed.**

- **The rule.** `StaffIdentityAdministration.decide` refuses the maker (`SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN`, still the last refusal) only when `meetsTier(authorized.grant?.tier, 'P')` is false. **Migration `0032_staff_self_decision`** drops the CHECK `staff_identity_checker_is_not_maker` (a CHECK sees only the row) and adds the trigger `staff_identity_transition_checker` (`melarc.staff_identity_checker_guard`, an AFTER insert or update trigger, so that it refuses where the CHECK did: after the policies and the other constraints; the first form, a BEFORE trigger, changed which refusal the bootstrap policies' own test sees and was caught by the gate): when a checker is written and is the maker, the row is not a bootstrap identity, and the maker's bundle holds no grant of `staff.identity.approve` at tier `P`, the write is refused with `23514` and the old constraint name, so the table still holds the rule for every other writer. A maker the table cannot find fails closed.
- **The documents, once at the owner and by reference elsewhere.** [permissions.md](../../contracts/permissions.md) §6 states the exception (the one owner); the master specification §11.5, §11.6, §29.2, §30.8, §35.12.2 and §37.4, [errors-and-enums.md](../../contracts/errors-and-enums.md), [audit.md](../../contracts/audit.md), [state-machines.md](../../contracts/state-machines.md), [domain-model.md](../../contracts/domain-model.md), `openapi.yaml` (descriptions of `approveStaffIdentity`, `createStaffIdentity`, `approveOnePackageException`, `approveBundleChange`, `decideAdjustmentResolution`, `createVendorOrganization`, `decideVendorOrganization` and the bundle list; no schema, code, status or key changed, and the client was regenerated and compared), the feature criteria (`AC-SLICE-000-85`, `-117`, `-118` and `-122` retitled or reworded, `AC-VENDOR-03`, `AC-RETURN-05`, `AC-ADJUST-05`, `AC-SLICE-001-03`, `AC-SLICE-001-55`; ids unchanged), [SECURITY_DESIGN.md](../../architecture/SECURITY_DESIGN.md) §5, [MIGRATION_AND_SEEDING.md](../../architecture/MIGRATION_AND_SEEDING.md) §3 (the first profile; the pair is kept for custody and recovery, not for the approval), the Ops Portal surface and patterns, `SLICE-000.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md` and the two area `CLAUDE.md` files.
- **The Ops Portal.** The profile's page offers the maker the approve and reject acts with a note ("You created this profile. A Platform Admin can approve or reject a profile they made; anyone else needs a different person to."), and the sentences that said a different person must approve (the status line, the add-profile page and its success, the menu description) now say the profile is approved, by a different approver unless the maker is a Platform Admin. The refusal sentence of `approveStaffIdentity` says only a Platform Admin can decide a profile they made.
- **The hubs.** `currentSessionOf` lists every hub when the snapshot holds a grant of the all-hub scope (a Platform Admin, and Finance for `vendor.read`), by name; `authorized_hub_ids` stays what the session was issued with. The landing page's empty sentence is again only "No hub is listed for your session." and the add-profile hub field is a real choice for a Platform Admin. The contract text of `authorized_hubs` says so.
- **The readiness.** `ReferenceDataReadiness` (`reference-data-readiness.ts`; registered wherever a database is composed, not in the inert composition) reads the role bundles and the settings under the `authentication` capability and throws `NotReadyError('reference_data_missing')`; a database that does not answer stays `dependency_unavailable`. A new coarse reason in `NotReadyReason`; the probe's precedence is `dependency_unavailable`, then `reference_data_missing`, then `policy_superseded`. [DEPLOYMENT_AND_ENVIRONMENTS.md](../../architecture/DEPLOYMENT_AND_ENVIRONMENTS.md) and `DEVELOPMENT.md` say so. **The gate caught three consequences the first tests had missed**: the real-process tests of `api-process.db.test.ts` started the built API over an unseeded database and expected it ready (an earlier run of them had used a stale `dist`), so they now seed first and one new test proves the real process goes from `reference_data_missing` to ready with no restart; the integrated harness's database was never seeded, so its API could not become ready, and `e2e-database create` gained an opt-in `--seed` (the real seed, as the provisioning login, its output kept off the tool's one line of JSON; a database that cannot be seeded is dropped) which `createDatabase()` of the harness now asks for; and the first form of the maker-checker trigger (BEFORE) refused before the row-level-security policies and changed the answer the bootstrap policies' own test pins (`42501`), so it is an AFTER trigger. The generated client had also been left stale by a later edit of the contract's wording, which `api-client:check` caught.
- **The favicon.** The owner saw `tmp/favicon-candidate/preview.png` (git-ignored: the supplied symbol, byte for byte, `melarc-symbol.svg`, SHA-256 `5bd8d85c…8c95`, at tab sizes on a light and a dark tab, where its black part nearly disappears) and **approved it as it is, in the same conversation**. It is wired as `apps/ops-web/public/favicon.svg` (a byte-for-byte copy) and one `<link rel="icon">` in `index.html`; the brand README, `BRAND_FOUNDATION.md` and `apps/ops-web/CLAUDE.md` record the approval **for the Ops Portal's browser-tab icon alone** (no app icon, installable icon or other use); `test/favicon.test.ts` and `test/build.test.ts` pin the copy, the checksum, the single link and the shipped file; and the browser tests no longer allow a `404` for `/favicon.ico`, so a missing icon would fail them.
- **The leftover databases.** `db:orphans --drop` removed the five `melarc_test_*` databases (none had a session); none remain.

**Rulings.**

1. **The exemption is the tier of the acting grant (P), because "authorize on held permissions, never role names".** A bundle's name and its `privileged` flag are not it: Senior Ops is privileged and holds the approval at tier S.
2. **The rule is stated once, in `permissions.md` §6, and every other document points to it** rather than restating it (each fact has one owning document).
3. **The table holds the rule where it can.** A trigger that reads the maker's bundle grant replaces the CHECK, so a writer that is not the application is held to the same rule; it is checked when the checker is written, and fails closed for a maker it cannot find.
4. **The page cannot tell a Platform Admin from another maker**, because the session lists permission keys and no tiers and the contract says the client never decides from them. The maker is offered the acts with a plain note and the server refuses anyone else; hiding the buttons, as before, would have hidden them from the Platform Admin too.
5. **The bootstrap pair stays.** Two custodians keep the two administrators apart and each administrator's authenticator is reset by the other; only the reason that the first profile needed the second administrator is gone, and `MIGRATION_AND_SEEDING.md` step 6 and its "who approves the first profile" paragraph are rewritten accordingly.
6. **`reference_data_missing` is a reason of its own**, because its remedy (run the seed) is not the remedy of a dependency that does not answer (wait), as the two existing reasons are told apart by remedy.
7. **No new audit field.** `staff.identity.approved` already records `created_by` and `approved_by`; for a Platform Admin's own decision they are one identity, which is what makes the exception as checkable as the rule.

**Findings for the Product Owner.**

1. **The decision reaches further than staff profiles in the documents.** "Every approval" now means a Platform Admin may also decide a bundle change they proposed (`permission.bundle.approve`, the act the contract calls the one that can manufacture every other authority), an adjustment resolution, a return-fee waiver, a one-package exception, a vendor activation and a price correction they made. None of those operations is built (SLICE-001 and later; `approveBundleChange` is SLICE-009), so no code differs yet, and each slice applies the rule when it is built. **Say if any of them (the bundle change and the money ones most of all) should keep a second person.**
2. **A Senior Ops maker is offered the buttons and refused after pressing one.** The page cannot know the tier (ruling 4). Showing the right thing needs the session to carry the tier of each permission it lists, which is a change to `CurrentSession`; say if you want it.
3. **A Platform Admin's own approval raises no alert.** It is audited like any other (the same two ids), and nothing flags it. If you want a flag in the audit trail or a report of self-approvals, that is a small addition.
4. **The first administrator can now approve the first profile alone.** The second administrator still matters for custody and for the reset of an authenticator.
5. **The favicon is wired, as you approved it. On a dark browser tab its black part nearly disappears** (the red blocks stay). If that bothers you, supply or approve a variant for dark tabs (the white logo you supplied is the whole logo, not the symbol); an `<link media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">` would choose between the two.
6. **Your database needs the migration, and the API needs a rebuild and a restart.** `db:migrate` applies `0032` (forward-only; nothing is dropped but the one CHECK). Until the API is rebuilt and restarted it still refuses a Platform Admin their own approval, and the page already offers it.

**Tests added or changed.** `staff-maker-checker.db.test.ts` (the table's rule: refused for a Senior Ops, Ops Staff and Finance maker, and for a maker that is no identity; allowed for a Platform Admin maker, to approve and to reject, for an ordinary and a privileged bundle; reads the tier of the approval and no other grant; holds for a row written directly), `staff-administration-routes.db.test.ts` (a Platform Admin approves their own profile whatever its role, with one setup grant, one message and an event naming one identity twice; rejects their own with a reason; a Senior Ops maker is refused to approve and to reject; the privileged rejection by the maker; the hubs a session lists, two tests), `bootstrap-journey.db.test.ts` (the first profile: approved by its maker, and approved by the other administrator, two tests), `reference-data-readiness.test.ts` (new, 5), `health.test.ts` (the new reason and its precedence, 3), `reference-data-readiness.db.test.ts` (new, 2: not ready then ready on a real database, and live throughout) and `integration-kit.db.test.ts` (three tests now expect the truthful answer of an unseeded database), `api-process.db.test.ts` (the three real-process tests seed first; one new test: live, then `reference_data_missing`, then ready after the seed with no restart), `e2e-database-tool.db.test.ts` (new, 3: no seeding unless asked, the reference data with `--seed`, any other argument refused and nothing created) and the harness's `database.test.ts` (it asks for `create --seed`); in the Ops Portal the profile (the maker is offered the acts and told who may; a person who did not make it is not told they did; the refusal sentence; the status line), the add-profile page (its description and its success), the words of deciding a profile, the landing and the session flow (the empty-hubs sentence), and `staff.spec.ts` (the maker approves their own profile in a real browser, in the production build and in the development server).

### 7.43 Carried from the owner's design decisions of 25 October 2026

**Why.** On the same day, while the decisions of [§7.42](#742-carried-from-the-owners-decisions-of-25-october-2026) were being built, the owner redirected the look of the Ops Portal in three messages: *"this is not a website hence the nav bar is not suppose to be at the top. We need a sliding/collasable side menu (screenshot example given). Also pull icons into the design system and use it. Use Icons but be consistent with it. For instance the show password needs am eye icon not a text and a button. Lucide/Flaticons has Icons, integrate into our project and wire it be used entire for our project"* (with the reference screenshot of a dark menu: the mark and the name, a collapse button, entries with icons, a red current item, and an account card with a sign-out icon at the foot); *"the athentication screen needs to be Split-Screen Layouts. I will put the images design/images"*; and, with the photographs in place, *"screens"*. Nothing is staged, committed or pushed.

**What changed.**

- **The navigation is a side menu, not a band** (`components/side-menu/`, `AuthenticatedOpsShell`; COMPONENT_PATTERNS §12.6). Ink, 16rem, full height; a collapse button turns it into a rail of icons (4.5rem) with every name kept; on a screen under 48rem a slim bar with a menu button stands in its place and the menu slides in over an inert page (Escape, the scrim, the close button and following a link close it, focus goes in and comes back). The account card at the foot names the person, says where they act and holds the sign-out icon. The old `ShellBar` is gone.
- **Three frame layouts** (`neutral`, `sidebar`, `split`), chosen by the route tree through `useFrameLayout` and never by a page (`app/frame-chrome.ts`, `AppFrame`). The sidebar layout draws no banner; the menu carries the name.
- **Icons: Lucide, through one door** (`lucide-react` 1.58.0 exact, ISC licence text in `public/licenses/`; `components/ui/icon/icons.ts` is the only file that imports it, named by meaning; `Icon` and `IconButton`; DESIGN_SYSTEM §24, COMPONENT_PATTERNS §22). Used in the menu, the account card, the status pictures, the sort arrows, the pager and **the password field's eye** ("Show password" is an open eye, "Hide password" a crossed one, with no text). A test fails on a second importer, a hand-drawn `<svg>`, an unused icon and a name the registry lacks; ESLint says the same.
- **The split screen for the five pre-sign-in screens** (`AuthSplitLayout`, `components/auth-art/`; DESIGN_SYSTEM §13.1a): from 64rem the photograph fills the left half over a band of Ink with the mark and the name, and the banner and form are in the right half, in a column of at most 30rem. The four photographs of `design/images` are served as web-sized WebP copies with no metadata (`src/assets/auth/`, checksums in its README, `test/auth-art.test.ts`); one table says which goes with which screen (`auth-art.ts`).
- **Tests and tokens.** Two layout tokens (`sidebar-width`, `sidebar-width-collapsed`) and the pairings of the menu are registered, so `design-tokens.test.ts` and the contrast tests cover them; the Ops unit tests, `shell.spec.ts`, `components.spec.ts`, `pre-sign-in.spec.ts` and `staff.spec.ts` were rewritten for the new design.

**Rulings.**

1. **The symbol is the mark of the menu and of the split screen's band, provisionally.** The reference screenshot shows a mark and the name; the only symbol the owner has approved is the favicon, for the browser-tab alone. `BrandLockup` draws that file on a white tile (black on Ink would vanish) with the name as text, and the brand README and `BRAND_FOUNDATION.md` record this use as **owner to confirm**; `favicon.test.ts` fails if the code and the record part.
2. **The split screen's form column is 30rem**, which is about 430 px of form at 1280 and in a narrow window, and so narrower than the 560 to 720 px of DESIGN_SYSTEM §13.3; that section says "generally" and now states the exception.
3. **A web copy of each photograph, not the original** (6 to 12 MB each): resized to 1800 px, metadata dropped (the camera, place and time do not go to a visitor), WebP; the originals stay in `design/images/`. Which photograph goes with which screen is my choice, in one table.
4. **The menu's collapsed state lives in memory only.** The application may not use web storage (ESLint), so a reload expands it. A remembered choice would need a server-held preference.
5. **The whole panel scrolls when the window is too short**, rather than pinning the account card and squeezing the entries (see the defects below). Tooltips are the native `title`, repeating the accessible name; no custom tooltip is built, because a hover or focus tooltip has to be dismissible, hoverable and persistent (WCAG 1.4.13).
6. **The photograph loads lazily**, so a screen too narrow to draw it never downloads it.

**Defects the real-browser pass found, each fixed after a failing test.**

1. Under reduced motion the open menu still slid: the rule of the open state (specificity 0,3,0) beat the `prefers-reduced-motion` rule (0,1,0).
2. At 200% text on a 320 px screen the product's name was crushed into a column of single letters beside the mark, the menu's head grew to 489 px, the entries were squeezed to 48 px and the account card spilled out of the panel. The head and the lockup now wrap, the whole panel scrolls, and the docked menu is never wider than half the window.
3. A 390 px phone downloaded the photograph (58 to 266 KB) it never draws.
4. The showcase's icon grid (mine) and its surfaces grid (older, never measured at 200%) made the page scroll sideways at 320 px with enlarged text.
5. The browser tests' `reachableNames` counted controls a keyboard cannot reach (hidden, or inside something inert); it no longer does.

**Findings for the Product Owner.**

1. **Confirm the symbol as the mark of the menu and of the split screen** (ruling 1), or send the mark you want there.
2. **The photographs' licence and attribution are yours to confirm**; the repository does not know them. Say if one should not be used, or goes with another screen (`auth-art.ts`).
3. **The form is about 430 px wide in the split screen** (ruling 2). Say if you want it wider, up to the 560 to 720 px.
4. **A reload expands a collapsed menu** (ruling 4).
5. **At 200% text on the smallest screen the sign-out icon is below the fold of the open menu** until it is scrolled to; Firefox, unlike the other two, does not scroll a partly visible control into view on focus.
6. **The narrow-screen bar is the page's banner landmark**; the development showcase, which also has the frame's banner, therefore has two under 48rem (development only).
7. **A session with no display name reads "Signed in" in the card and "You are signed in." on the landing.**

**Tests added or changed.** Ops unit tests for the icon registry and `Icon`, `IconButton`, `SideMenu`, `PrimaryNavigation`, the shell, the frame's three layouts, the split layout and the photographs; `icon-registry.test.ts`, `auth-art.test.ts`, `favicon.test.ts` (the provisional use), `navigation-no-roles.test.ts`; the eslint rules test; in a real browser, in three engines: `shell.spec.ts` (the menu beside the page, its icons and account card, the Tab walk with the collapse button, collapse and expand with the page taking the room and nothing stored, the narrow bar and its closed-and-open states, Escape, the scrim, the close button, reduced motion, 200% text, forced colours, axe at 1280, 768 and 320 px in each state), `components.spec.ts` (the demo menu), `pre-sign-in.spec.ts` (the split screen at 1280, 800 and 390 px, the lazy photograph, the eye by keyboard, the form's column) and `staff.spec.ts` (the shell in its two forms at the verified widths).

**Gate** (25 October 2026, uncached, `TURBO_FORCE=true`, Node 24.21.0, Windows, once on the frozen tree, `tmp/gate-s045-main.log`): `install`, `format:check`, `typecheck`, `build` (Ops bundle 486.87 kB, 150.17 kB gzipped), `contract:check` (17 operations, no findings), `api-client:check`, `db:check` and `test:db` (2907 passed, 2 skipped, 93 files) exit 0; the browser suite in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit exit 0 (1035 passed, 6 skipped, 27 minutes) and `test:e2e` exit 0 (20 passed); `pnpm audit --audit-level high` exit 0 (one moderate advisory, as before). **Two stages failed and were corrected, and the tree changed after the gate by those corrections alone**: `lint` (a style error in a test of mine, and a scratch folder of mine under the git-ignored `tmp/` that ESLint reaches) and `test:local`, whose failures were: the documentation guard (`agent-docs`: a path in `apps/ops-web/CLAUDE.md` that did not exist, and the photographs' README linked from no `CLAUDE.md`), `identity-decisions.test.ts` (it still pinned the old rule that a privileged rejection needs a Platform Admin *other than the maker*, against the contract text of §7.42) and `database.module.test.ts` (an unreachable database now also fails the `reference-data` check, which the warning lists). After the corrections, `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck` and `test:local` exit 0 (root 1245 passed and 2 skipped; Ops 2030 in 103 files; API 5793 passed and 12 skipped in 199 files; api-client 250; harness 482 passed and 3 skipped). The corrections touch two tests, one test's narrowing and two documents: **`test:db`, the browser suite and `test:e2e` were not run again after them.** The race tests of `staff-sign-in.db.test.ts` that failed intermittently with `DatabaseDeadlineError` while the migration was being weighed (1.5 s lock hold against a 2 s lock timeout) passed in this run; the cause is not found.

**On the real stack** (a disposable database, the real seeds and bootstrap, the real API and the real Vite, real Chromium; nothing secret printed; screenshots in `tmp/screens-real/`): both bootstrap administrators did the setup and the two-step sign-in through the split screen with no console or API error; the sign-in at 1280 px has the photograph in the left half (640 px, loaded, 1800 px wide) and the eye toggles the password (an icon button with no text, "Show password" then "Hide password"); at 800 and 390 px the photograph is not drawn; signed in, the side menu is 256 px wide, has no banner above the page, lists Overview, Staff, Add a staff profile and Sessions with icons and the account card, collapses to 72 px and opens as a drawer at 390 px; the add-profile form offers the hub; and **one Platform Admin created a profile and approved it alone**. Not run on the real stack: the transition of `/readyz` from `reference_data_missing` to ready (the real-process database test proves it), the delivery worker, and a second device or engine other than Chromium. Migration `0032` was then applied to the owner's `melarc_dev` (`db:migrate`: 1 migration); the owner's API must be rebuilt and restarted to use the new rule.

**The approval flow, audited after the owner reported it not working on their machine** (25 October 2026, later). Three facts about *their* stack, found before anything was changed on it: (1) their `melarc_dev` still held the old CHECK `staff_identity_checker_is_not_maker` until the `db:migrate` above (it had 32 migrations and now has 33; the CHECK is gone and the trigger `staff_identity_transition_checker` is present), so the database itself refused a maker's approval whatever the code said; (2) their API process of 10:25 predated the rebuild of 14:18 (they restarted it at 14:30, after the rebuild and the migration, so it now runs the new code on the migrated database); (3) **the delivery worker is not running there**, so an approval, even a successful one, queues a setup link that nobody sends, while the page says "A setup link is on its way". The whole chain was then run on a fresh disposable stack with the final code **and the worker**: one Platform Admin made a profile and approved it alone, the worker delivered the message, the colleague followed the link, set a password and signed in; and a second administrator approved a profile the first had made. Both worked, with no console or API error. Not reproduced: the exact failure they saw (the old CHECK and an unmigrated database were not recreated); the diagnosis is the three facts above.

**For the Product Owner (the approval flow).** The API and the database are now current; start the worker (`pnpm --filter @melarc/api run start:worker:local`; its messages are files in `DELIVERY_CAPTURE_DIRECTORY`, by default `~/.melarc/capture`, where the link is), and open `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. **Finding:** the success sentence promises a link that exists only while a worker runs; if you want, the page or the first-sign-in section of `DEVELOPMENT.md` can say so where the person is looking.

## 9. Stop conditions and the task handoff

**Stop conditions** are those of the [runbook](BOOTSTRAP_B0_RUNBOOK.md#7-stop-conditions), and also stop the task when: a decision contradicts a retained document it does not override; a product value a task needs is unset (surface it, never default it); a change would break a stable identifier; `contract:check` or `api-client:check` fails for a reason not traceable to the task's own edit; a step needs a machine trust-store or global tool change; the task would touch unrelated work; a port cannot be placed without a new domain; a deadlock appears in a concurrency run (the lock order is then a specification defect for the owner); a package or tool is not already approved.

**Handoff.** End each task in the runbook's [format](BOOTSTRAP_B0_RUNBOOK.md#8-task-handoff-format), extended for this slice:

```text
Task: S0.NN, title
Git: HEAD, branch, and the scope of uncommitted change
Files changed:
Decisions implemented (document and section):
Commands run (exact) and exit codes:
Result: the affected run's closing lines as printed (passed, failed, owed); counts; every skipped test with its reason and the environment it needs
Evidence reached, per criterion: fixture/platform verified, or real-operation verified
Obligations closed, and obligations carried (OB-nn)
Checks not run, and why (services, browser, platform; the gate, unless the owner asked for it)
Problem or blocker, if any:
Findings the Product Owner must decide: conflicts, provisional values, suggestions
```

Raw logs are kept only when they help debugging or CI.
